title: How to Measure Your Company's Process Maturity
summary: How to measure your company's process maturity in 2026: indicators, maturity levels, and how Jestor helps you track it.
body_markdown:
Process maturity measures how documented, standardized, automated, and monitored with real data a company's workflows are. Measuring this maturity helps decide where to invest first in process management.


Many managers know their operation has bottlenecks but have no clear way to measure them. The result is investing in automation in the wrong place, without understanding the real root cause.


Assessing process maturity before any BPM project prevents wasting time and budget on solutions that don't target the right bottleneck.


## Signs of low process maturity


- Processes exist only in a few people's heads
- There's no data on average task execution time
- Each department works with different, disconnected tools
- Approvals depend on informal contact, with no defined workflow
- Errors keep repeating without anyone investigating the cause


## How to assess your maturity level


- Check whether processes are documented and accessible to the team
- Measure whether there are time, cost, and volume indicators per process
- Check the level of automation already present in each workflow
- Assess whether historical data exists to support decisions
- Ask the team whether the process is actually followed in practice


## How to advance your process maturity


- Prioritize critical processes with the highest volume or impact
- Create simple indicators before moving on to complex automations
- Standardize workflows with clear steps and owners
- Automate repetitive tasks identified during the assessment
- Review indicators periodically to measure real progress

## Frequently asked questions


**Why measure process maturity?** To direct automation investment to where the real bottlenecks are. See an example at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Which indicators should you measure first?** Average execution time, task volume, and rework rate per process are usually a good place to start.


**Does low maturity mean the company is behind?** Not necessarily. It's a common starting point that objectively guides the next steps.


Regularly measuring process maturity turns operations management into a practice based on data, not guesswork.
